transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump is going to Nebraska today to campaign for Republican Senator Pete Ricketts.
The GOP incumbent is facing a strong challenge from independent candidate Dan Osborne, who
is backed by national Democrats.
Vice President Vance is going to Fairbanks, Alaska today to support GOP candidates.
Trump's presidential election will go to a run-off vote later this month.
None of the leading candidates got more than 50 percent of the ballots.
The son of a former far-right Brazilian president, Flavio Bolsonaro, is leading the left-wing
incumbent Luis Inacio Lula da Silva.
And Pierre's carry-con reports from Rio de Janeiro the results are very close.
Flavio Bolsonaro won with 47 percent of the vote.
Is the 45-year-old eldest son of Jair Bolsonaro, who was barred from running this time he was
convicted of flooding a coup to overturn the 2022 election?
The current president, who is 80 years old, Lula, received 45 percent of the vote.
And Pierre's carry-con reporting.
Russian authorities are playing down reports of an outbreak of the plague in Siberia.
Concerns arose last week after a worker at a Siberian institute dedicated to the study
of the plague and other infectious diseases died of a mysterious illness.
From Moscow, NPR's Charles Mains has details.
Russia's consumer health watchdog, Ross Patreb-Nazor, said the victim was a 28-year-old female lab
worker at an anti-plague research facility in the Irkutsk region, who had succumbed to
pneumonia of an unknown origin.
The local governor has since announced a state-run investigation, found no pathogens in the lab
technician's body linked to her professional activities, and pronounced the epidemiological
situation in the wider Irkutsk region stable.
Yet that statement was at odds with as-yet-unconfirmed local media reports several hospitals were
under quarantine amid concerns over the spread of the mnemonic plague, a potentially lethal
airborne disease that was a focus of study at the Siberian lab.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow.
Stocks open mix this morning as OPEC and its allies agree to keep oil production steady.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones industrial average slipped about 200 points
in early trading.
OPEC and other major oil-producing countries said over the weekend they will continue pumping
crude oil at current levels through November.
Crude oil prices remain elevated, with the international benchmark hovering above $100
a barrel.
Energy prices have also been pushed higher by a shortage of refining capacity.
Ukraine says it sidelined more than half of Russia's refining ability.
Retail gasoline and diesel prices in the U.S. have fallen by more than a dime a gallon in
the last week.
Government bond yields continue to climb, and that's making it more expensive for anyone
else trying to borrow money.
The yield on 10-year treasuries, which affects the cost of mortgages and other loans, has
risen to about 5.3 percent.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
This is NPR.
Lawyers for condemned prisoner Krista Pike say she remains hospitalized in Tennessee
after her failed execution last week.
She is unconscious and on a ventilator.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has named former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton to lead an investigation.
The governor also says the state's corrections commissioner Frank Strada will resign this
month.
Lawyers opposed to the death penalty say Strada has now overseen two botched executions in
Tennessee and three previous botched executions in Arizona.
One American and two German scientists were awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology
or Medicine today, and Beers-Robstein reports it's for their fundamental discoveries that
help explain how the brain works.
The Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute in Sweden awarded the prize to two German
scientists, Peter Hegeman and Gerd Nagel, and one American, Karl Deisserhof, at Stanford
University.
The three scientists played key roles in discoveries that led to light-controlled switches that
turned nerve cells on and off.
The technique opened a new way to understand the function of neurons known as optogenetics.
The Nobel Committee says the discoveries laid the foundation for a new era of neuroscience,
including helping you understand how the brain forms memories, feelings, and behaviors.
Rob Stein, NPR News.
Their authorities in California say the bouquet fire north of Los Angeles has scorched more
than a mile.
There are evacuation orders posted.
This is NPR.
This message comes from Lisa and their lineup of beautifully crafted mattresses tailored
to how you sleep.
Each mattress is made with eco-friendly materials and designed with specific sleep positions
and fuel preferences in mind.

That's L-E-E-S-A.com promo code NPR for up to 30% off mattresses plus an extra $50 off.
